_comment: Mapping from OnTheIssues' 24-topic vocabulary to the product's 19 issue
categories. This is an EDITORIAL artefact, not a derived fact: several of
the joins are arguable and some are many-to-one. It lives in its own file
so it can be argued about and revised without touching scraper code.
Two honest gaps are recorded rather than papered over:
unmapped_source_topics  - OnTheIssues topics with no product category
unpopulated_categories  - product categories no OnTheIssues topic feeds
Forcing either to zero would mean inventing a correspondence.

Principles & Values: OnTheIssues uses this for religion, ideology and general political
philosophy. It has no clean counterpart in the product taxonomy —
'Constitutional Issues' is about court appointments and executive
power, which is a different thing. Mapping it there would file a
candidate's statements about faith under separation of powers.
Kept and surfaced under its own name instead.

unpopulated_categories.Constitutional Issues: no OnTheIssues source topic; see Principles & Values note
unpopulated_categories.International Development and Human Righ: partially inside Foreign Policy, but not separable at source

many_to_one: Economy and Finance draws on four source topics; Foreign Policy and
Social Justice on three each. A category's quote count is therefore a
sum across topics and is not comparable to a single-topic category.
crime_placement: 'Crime' is filed under Social Justice and Civil Rights because the
product taxonomy puts Criminal Justice Reform and Police Reform there.
OnTheIssues uses the topic for both reform and enforcement positions,
so the category mixes both stances.
